title: Merchant Lending — Onboarding Criteria & Prompt Suite (Private Data)
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects the customer-specific evaluation pack for Merchant Lending Co. (enterprise banking partner). It bundles the pinned prompt suite, private dataset inventory, explicit acceptance criteria for model onboarding, and the sign-off checklist. Use this as the canonical artifact for the applied-ml handoff to release and SRE for production rollout.

Scope and constraints:
- Model variants under evaluation: gptx-legacy-35b-quant, opensim-40b-fp16, and rl-calibrated-13b-q4 (internal aliases).
- Private customer dataset: MerchantLendingQA-v2 (see dataset inventory below). Data is PII-sanitized CSV delivered via secure SFTP.
- Tests are run in the staging VPC private world; no customer data leaves the VPC.
- This is a working document: expect iterative updates after each eval run.

Owner / Contacts:
- Applied-ML owner: Elena R. Soto (elena@redwood.ai)
- Solutions lead at customer: Andrew Park (Merchant Lending Co.)
- Release liaison: Marcus Li
- Security reviewer: Priya Narang

Dataset inventory (private):
- MerchantLendingQA-v2.csv — 12,480 rows. Columns: case_id, prompt_context, question, expected_answer, business_label, sensitivity_flag. Sensitive rows were redacted following the contract; original PII mapping retained only in customer's environment.
- Historical-Disputes-2022.parquet — subset (3k) for edge-case dispute language.
- Synthetic-augmentations.jsonl — 8k synthetic variations we generated to cover phrasing variation (seeded with customer examples).

Pinned prompt suite (locked for regression tests):
1) triage_summary_v1:
   - Prompt: "Customer message: \n   {{prompt_context}}\n   In 3 sentences, summarize the core issue and recommended next step for merchant operations. Use neutral tone, avoid legal advice."
   - Rationale: canonical short-turn summarization used by merchant ops UI.
2) decision_boundary_check_v2:
   - Prompt: "Given the case: {{question}}. Does this case meet criteria for automatic chargeback reversal? Answer YES/NO and include 1-line rationale referencing business_label."
   - Rationale: binary decision with explainability.
3) escalation_reasoning_v1:
   - Prompt: "Compose an escalation note (two bullet points) a specialist can use to investigate a high-risk dispute. Include missing evidence checklist."

Note: Prompts must not be changed between regression runs; if we adjust a prompt, we record a new prompt id and rebaseline.

Evaluation metrics and acceptance criteria (per contract):
- Accuracy (answer match vs. expected_answer): >= 87% on MerchantLendingQA-v2 overall.
- Precision on "YES" decision for chargeback reversal: >= 0.91 (to limit false reversals).
- Recall on "flag-for-escalation" label: >= 0.85 (minimize missed high-risk cases).
- Summary quality: human-rated fluency score >= 4.2/5 (n=200 sample, blinded).
- Hallucination rate: factual hallucinations <= 4% measured on curated 500-case audit set (disputes/historical).
- Latency (99th percentile for inference on default batch size): <= 300ms for dedicated capacity; <= 650ms on shared hosted during peak simulation.
- Token cost: relative token cost delta vs. benchmark model must be <= +18% for chosen variant.

Regression test plan (automated + human):
- Automated: run eval harness (scripts/run_customer_eval.sh) that executes the pinned prompts against MerchantLendingQA-v2 and synthetic augmentations; produces confusion matrices and per-prompt pass/fail.
- Smoke: run on small staging subset (1k rows) after any model or infra change.
- Human eval: sampling 200 cases across buckets (normal / edge / disputes) for fluency and hallucination annotation. Annotators: 2 redwood annotators + 1 merchant SME; majority vote final.
- Failure classification: each failing case must be labeled as one of: behavior-regression, latency-violation, cost-violation, or data-misalignment.

Baseline and artifact naming convention:
- Use artifact tag format: merchantlending/<model-alias>/<YYYYMMDD>-run-<runid>. Example: merchantlending/opensim-40b/20250818-run-17
- Store evaluation outputs in internal S3 bucket with path: s3://redwood-evals/merchantlending/<run-tag>/results.csv (note: access control needed).

Sign-off criteria and workflow:
- Required pass: all acceptance metrics met OR documented compensating controls approved by security and product.
- Stakeholder sign-offs required (name and timestamp):
  - Applied-ML owner (Elena Soto)
  - Product PM (Merchant features) — Theo Alvarez
  - Security/compliance reviewer — Priya Narang
  - Customer success / customer rep — Andrew Park
- To sign-off: attach the final eval artifact and the human-eval CSV; each signer must append a note in the Confluence page and reference the run-tag.

Run instructions (quick):
- Pull latest model container: scripts/pull_model.sh <model-alias>
- Start eval: scripts/run_customer_eval.sh --model <model-alias> --data-path /mnt/secure/merchantlending/MerchantLendingQA-v2.csv --prompts pinned_prompts.json --outdir /tmp/eval-out/<run-tag>
- Upload results: scripts/publish_eval.sh --in /tmp/eval-out/<run-tag> --tag <run-tag>

Open questions / TODOs (working notes):
- Confirm whether the customer wants deterministic decoding for decision_boundary_check_v2; customer engineering is leaning toward greedy for auditability. (Action: Marcus to confirm by 2025-08-22).
- We should consider an adversarial prompt sweep for PCI/PHI trigger phrases — not yet scheduled.
- Determine retention policy for human-eval annotations (legal to confirm).

Rollback & mitigation playbook (if onboarded model regresses post-launch):
- Roll to previous run-tag via routing rules in Console (A/B rollback route to previous stable variant).
- Temporarily enable stricter threshold in product (force manual review for YES decisions).
- Notify customer and open incident ticket referencing JIRA-ENG-1462.

Appendix: exemplar pinned_prompts.json (abbreviated)
{
  "triage_summary_v1": "Customer message: {{prompt_context}}\\nIn 3 sentences, summarize the core issue and recommended next step for merchant operations. Use neutral tone, avoid legal advice.",
  "decision_boundary_check_v2": "Given the case: {{question}}. Does this case meet criteria for automatic chargeback reversal? Answer YES/NO and include 1-line rationale referencing business_label.",
  "escalation_reasoning_v1": "Compose an escalation note (two bullet points) a specialist can use to investigate a high-risk dispute. Include missing evidence checklist."
}

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally includes both automated thresholds and human review path to reflect the customer contract. If you update acceptance numbers, add a short justification and link the supporting analysis.
- I will run a full baseline eval on 2025-08-21 and attach artifacts.

End of document.
